title: HiST: Hierarchical Semantic Tree Augmentation for Generative Recommendation

problem.claim: Generative recommendation tokenization can exhibit semantic branch drift, assigning semantically similar items to different branches and causing information loss in generated semantic IDs.

gap.claim: Existing tokenization methods do not adequately bridge the semantic gap caused by semantic branch drift.

contributions.claim: HiST augments generative recommendation with hierarchical semantic tree information to bridge the semantic gap.
HiST constructs a semantic tree using a trained tokenizer, extracts hierarchical information bottom-up, and fuses it with original semantic IDs.
HiST uses separate prediction objectives for semantic IDs and hierarchical description components during end-to-end training.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe HiST as a novel framework and identify its core innovation as extracting and using hierarchical information from a semantic tree.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HiST significantly improves recommendation performance across multiple datasets.
The authors report consistent improvements when integrating HiST with various existing tokenization methods across evaluated settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommendation systems help users navigate large product catalogs, and generative recommendation has emerged as a flexible paradigm.
Different tokenization algorithms share the problem of semantic branch drift.
Semantic branch drift causes information loss in generated semantic IDs and reduces recommendation accuracy.
HiST constructs a hierarchical semantic tree, fuses its information with semantic IDs, and trains separate objectives for discrete structure and semantic relationships.
The authors report improvements across multiple datasets and consistent gains across tokenization methods and evaluated settings.

source_observation.claim: Semantic branch drift can separate semantically similar items and degrade the usefulness of generated semantic IDs.

interpretation.claim: Structured representations may benefit from explicitly preserving hierarchical relationships in addition to discrete identifiers.

application.claim: For generative recommendation systems, augment item identifiers with hierarchy-derived features and train objectives for both identifiers and hierarchical descriptions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy benefits domains, datasets, or tokenization methods beyond the evaluated settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated datasets, baselines, metrics, or improvement magnitudes.
The abstract does not describe the tokenizer architectures, training details, or computational costs.
The abstract does not provide ablations or failure cases.
